questions.question: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $\alpha^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
The velocity of sound in air depends on temperature as $v \propto \sqrt{T}$ (absolute temperature).
If the velocity doubles:
$\frac{v_2}{v_1} = 2 = \sqrt{\frac{T_2}{T_1}}$.
Squaring: $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = 4$.
With $T_1 = 0°C = 273.15$ K and $T_2 = 273.15 + \alpha$ K:
$\frac{273.15 + \alpha}{273.15} = 4$, giving $273.15 + \alpha = 1092.6$ K.
Therefore $\alpha = 819.45°C \approx 819°C$.

questions.solution:
The speed of a longitudinal wave in a solid is given by $v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$ where $Y$ is Young's modulus and $\rho$ is density.
Initial condition: $v_0 = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}} = 400$ m/s
After changes: $\rho' = 1.005\rho$ (0.5% increase) and $Y' = 1.01Y$ (1% increase)
New speed: $v' = \sqrt{\frac{Y'}{\rho'}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01Y}{1.005\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01}{1.005}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$
$\frac{v'}{v_0} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01}{1.005}} = \sqrt{1.00498...} \approx 1.00249$
$v' = 400 \times 1.00249 \approx 401$ m/s

questions.question: A closed organ pipe $150cm$ long gives $7$ beats per second with an open organ pipe of length $350cm$, both vibrating in fundamental mode. The velocity of sound is ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency in a closed pipe is given by

${f}_{c} = \dfrac{v}{4{l}_{1}} . . . \left(1\right)$

And, that in an open pipe is given by

${f}_{o} = \dfrac{v}{2{l}_{2}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Given that

$\left|{f}_{c} - {f}_{o}\right| = 7 . . . \left(3\right)$

questions.solution:
Frequency of sound heard by car-$1,$ which comes by reflection from car-$2$

${f}_{1} = {f}_{0}\left(\dfrac{340 + 2}{340 - 2}\right)\left(\dfrac{340 + 2}{340 - 2}\right)$

$= {f}_{0}\left(\dfrac{342}{338}\right)2$

Frequency of sound coming directly from car-$2$

${f}_{2} = {f}_{0}\left(\dfrac{340 + 2}{340 - 2}\right)$

$∴ {f}_{1} - {f}_{2} = {f}_{0}\left(\dfrac{342}{338}\right)\left(\dfrac{342}{338} - 1\right) = 8 . 09 ≃ 8Hz$

The formula to calculate the frequency $\left(f '\right)$ as heard by an observer with respect to the frequency $\left(f\right)$ produced from a source is given by

$f ' = \dfrac{v \pm {v}_{o}}{v ∓ {v}_{s}}f . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $v$ is the speed of sound in air, ${v}_{o}$ is the speed of the observer and ${v}_{s}$ is the speed of the source.

In the first situation, the source is the moving car and the observer is the wall. Hence, the frequency $\left({f}_{w}\right)$ as heard on the wall can be written as

$\begin{cases}{f}_{w} \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v - 0}{v - {v}_{c}}f \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{c}}f . . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

where, ${v}_{c}$ is the speed of the car.

In the second situation, when the sound reflects back from the wall, the source of sound is the wall and the observer is the car.

Hence, the frequency $\left({f}_{c}\right)$ of sound as heard by the car after the reflection is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - 0}{f}_{w} \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v}{f}_{w} . . . . ( 3 )\end{cases}$

From equation (2) and (3), it follows that

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v} \times \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{c}}f \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - {v}_{c}}f . . . . ( 4 )\end{cases}$
